In the overview below, you can quickly and easily find out for what purpose we collect which personal data from you, how long we keep this data, and who may receive this personal data from us.Execution of the membership agreement

If you become a member, we register your first and last name, address, date of birth, telephone number(s), email address, an NTTB number, for seniors the affinity with types of volunteer work, for youth members the address details of parents and/or guardians. During the membership, images and performance data are collected on a small scale. This data is available within the association for membership administration, the secretariat, and/or volunteers who organize activities (such as bar services). Outside the association, the data is made available to the NTTB and, if necessary, to subsidy providers (e.g., the municipality). We keep the data as long as you are a member and participate in any committees, and for some parts also from former members (see point 5).
Administration

In addition to the above data, your bank and payment details are recorded. These are accessible to the financial administration. This data is kept according to legal terms (currently for the financial administration for 7 years)
PR and communication

To inform you and others about activities and developments of T.T.V. Maastricht, we send newsletters, post messages on our website and on social media, etc. Where necessary and relevant, we only publish your name and images with your explicit consent. Upon registration or via a later provided consent form, you can indicate whether or not you agree with this.
Website

Every time you visit our website, cookies are placed to improve our digital services. The data is analyzed anonymously. The use of this data is strictly functional, and you do not have to give permission for this each time.
After termination of membership

If you are no longer a member, your contact details, as well as existing images and performance records, are kept for special events, reunions, etc. This material is available to the membership administration, the secretariat, and, for example, a reunion committee.

Cookies
A cookie is a small text file that is sent along with the pages of a website and stored by the browser on your computer, tablet, or mobile phone. We use cookies to provide you with more service when visiting our websites, making them easier to use. Cookies, for example, ensure that you can stay logged in to a website or that your preferences, such as location and language settings, are remembered. Thanks to cookies, we can see how often our websites—and which pages—are viewed by visitors. For certain cookies, you must first give permission before these cookies may be used. This permission is not required if and insofar as it concerns technically necessary (functional) cookies and analytical cookies, within the meaning of the applicable legislation, such as Article 11.7a paragraph 3 of the Telecommunications Act and the ePrivacy Regulation. You can always withdraw your consent for cookies by changing your internet settings. More information about enabling, disabling, and deleting cookies can be found in your browser's Help function.Provision of personal data to third partiesWithout your consent, the Association only provides your personal data to third parties if this is necessary or if the Association is legally obliged to provide your personal data to these third parties. In points 1 to 5 of the privacy statement, you will find an overview of the situations in which personal data is provided to third parties.

Access, correction, and deletion of personal data
You have the right to request the Association to access your personal data (unless the Association is not obliged to provide this access under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)) and to have your data supplemented, deleted, or blocked. You must identify yourself for such a request. If you wish your data to be deleted, the Association will pass on this deletion to all other organizations that have received the relevant data from the Association.Security of personal data
The Association takes appropriate measures to protect your personal data as well as possible against loss, unauthorized access, publication, and unlawful processing. We strive to ensure that only the necessary persons have access to your data, that access to personal data is shielded, and that our security measures are regularly checked.

Minors
If you wish to register as a minor, you must provide explicit permission from your parent or guardian.

Links to other websites
The website may contain links to other websites. This Privacy Statement only applies to the Association's websites. Other websites may have their own privacy policies. The Association advises you to always consult the privacy statement of those websites before using other websites.

Changes to the privacy policy
The Association adjusts its privacy policy from time to time to keep it up to date. The most recent version of our Privacy Statement will always be included on the websites. The Association therefore advises you to consult the Privacy Statement regularly. In case of important changes, the Association will do everything possible to inform you by email and via the websites.

Complaint about the processing of your personal data
